back_content: To travel on water in a ship or boat, or float smoothly through the air. Example: Boats sail gracefully on the river.
Structures built to span physical obstacles such as rivers or roads. Example: Beautiful stone bridges span across the water.
Stands higher than or rises above the top of something. Example: The rainbow overtops the tall forest trees.
The sky or firmament as viewed from earth. Example: The rainbow bridges earth to heaven.
More attractive or pleasing to look at. Example: Clouds sailing in the sky are prettier than river boats.
An arch or curved shape like a rainbow. Example: The bow that bridges heaven lights up the sky.
A band of colors produced by separation of light. Example: Sunlight forms a 7-color spectrum in raindrops.
Acronym for the 7 colors: Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red. Example: VIBGYOR helps us remember rainbow colors.
A transparent glass object that refracts light into spectrum colors. Example: Newton used a glass prism to split white light.
Relating to the atmosphere of the earth. Example: A rainbow is a glorious atmospheric optical phenomenon.
More beautiful, more attractive, lovelier. Example: The rainbow is prettier than man-made bridges.
Uglier, less attractive, plain. Example: Natural scenery is prettier, never ugly.
Float, glide, drift. Example: Clouds sail across the blue sky.
Earth / Ground. Example: The rainbow spans from earth to heaven.
Surpasses, exceeds, towers above. Example: The arch overtops the trees.
Demolish, destroy, dismantle. Example: The rainbow builds a bridge, human hands build stone arches.
Arch, curve, bend. Example: The colorful bow curved across the sky.
Compound word (/ˈreɪn.bəʊ/). Long 'a' sound in rain, long 'o' in bow.
Silent letter 'd' in bridge (/brɪdʒ/). The 'dg' together makes the '/dʒ/' sound.
Two syllables (/ˈhɛv.ən/). The 'ea' makes a short '/ɛ/' sound.
Two syllables (/ˈprɪt.i.ər/). Comparative suffix '-er' added after changing 'y' to 'i'.
Silent letters 'gh' in high (/haɪ/). The 'gh' is completely silent.
There is / There has. Example: There's a beautiful rainbow in the sky.
It is / It has. Example: It's prettier than any bridge on earth.
What is. Example: What's the third color in VIBGYOR?
Are not. Example: Aren't clouds prettier than boats on rivers?
Who is / Who has. Example: Who's the author of 'The Rainbow'?
To pursue unrealistic or impossible goals. Example: Don't just chase rainbows; work hard for your dreams.

front_content: At the end of the rainbow
back_content: A place of ultimate success or mythical wealth. Example: Legend says there is a pot of gold at the end of the rainbow.
To connect or bring two different things together. Example: The rainbow builds a bridge between earth and sky.
Extremely attractive and pleasing to look at. Example: The rainbow over the lake was as pretty as a picture.

front_content: All the colors of the rainbow
back_content: A wide and vibrant variety of colors. Example: The garden was filled with flowers of all the colors of the rainbow.
